visual_action: The video starts with a brief, grainy clip of Donald Trump walking on an airport tarmac and then appearing to climb the stairs to a plane. It then transitions to a long montage of clips featuring Barack Obama. The montage shows Obama in various settings: reading papers in the Oval Office, walking on a tarmac, smiling, having a drink with Anthony Bourdain in a restaurant, speaking at a podium with a 'VOTE' sign, speaking in front of an American flag, posing for a photo, dancing, walking with his dogs, interacting with a baby, drinking from a bottle, dancing with Michelle Obama, looking at a mural of Martin Luther King Jr., shaking hands with a service member, looking thoughtful, interacting with his family, awarding the Presidential Medal of Freedom to Joe Biden, playing with children on a playground, and pointing at the camera. Michelle Obama appears in several clips with him. The video ends with a close-up of Obama looking up, then fades to black.

cast.name: Barack Obama
cast.evidence: He is the subject of the entire montage that makes up the bulk of the video.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: The video opens with a clip of him, setting up a contrast with the subsequent montage of Barack Obama.

cast.name: Michelle Obama
cast.evidence: Appears in several clips alongside Barack Obama, including one where they are dancing.

cast.name: Joe Biden
cast.evidence: Shown receiving the Presidential Medal of Freedom from Barack Obama.

cast.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
cast.evidence: A large mural of his face is shown on a wall as Barack Obama looks at it.

spoken_summary: The audio consists solely of a song with the lyrics: "Crawlin' back to you... Never thought of crawlin' when you had a few... 'Cause I always do... Maybe I'm too busy bein' yours to fall for somebody new... Now I thought it through... Crawlin' back to you."
audio_music: A melancholic, romantic rock song plays throughout the video. It begins with the studio version of 'Do I Wanna Know?' by Arctic Monkeys, then transitions around the 8-second mark to a live cover version of the same song by Hozier, which continues for the rest of the clip. The music creates a sense of longing and nostalgia.
editing_pacing: The video is a fast-paced montage with quick cuts between various clips of Barack Obama, creating a dynamic and comprehensive portrait of his time in and out of office.
cultural_references: The soundtrack is the song 'Do I Wanna Know?' by the band Arctic Monkeys, with a mid-video switch to a cover by Hozier.
Chef and television personality Anthony Bourdain is shown having a meal and a drink with Barack Obama.
central_claim: The video implies that people are nostalgic for Barack Obama's presidency and want to 'crawl back' to the ideals he represents, especially when contrasted with Donald Trump.
intended_effect: To evoke feelings of fondness and nostalgia for Barack Obama and his presidency, thereby encouraging support for the Democratic party, while implicitly criticizing Donald Trump.
